messages:
Maya S: FYI — Frobnitz Inc opened a ticket: invoice #INV-2026-03-05 shows an 8.5% state sales tax line only on the one-time "setup fee". They provided a reseller certificate and PO. They say their bill-to entity is Frobnitz NY LLC (reseller), and tax_exempt=true on the customer record. Screenshot + PDF: https://files.frobnitz.example/INV-2026-03-05.pdf :eyes:

Liam B: ack. Do we have the raw invoice JSON / tax calculation log? My hunch: tax engine is mapping product code for setup_fee -> taxable by default.

Maya S: attached the invoice JSON from billing UI (pasted below) and the customer's PO. Quick paste: 
```
{
  "invoice_id": "INV-2026-03-05",
  "bill_to_entity": "Frobnitz NY LLC",
  "billing_country": "US",
  "line_items": [
    {"code":"usage","amount":1200.00,"taxable":false},
    {"code":"setup_fee","amount":250.00,"taxable":true}
  ],
  "tax_total": 21.25
}
```

Priya R: thanks. Customer claims `tax_exempt` is set on their account. Can someone confirm the customer record we used to render the invoice matched the PO (many customers have multiple entities). Maybe invoice selected a different "paying entity"?

Liam B: looking at billing-logs -- invoice renderer pulled paying_entity_id: pe_78b2 but the customer's reseller cert is tied to entity pe_78b1. So mismatch. That explains why setup_fee got taxed — pe_78b2 is in a different jurisdiction (NY vs. WA) and tax rules differ.

Arjun K: how did paying_entity_id get set to pe_78b2? Any recent changes in PO handling or defaulting for reserved capacity invoices?

Maya S: customer says they selected the PO that references Frobnitz NY LLC (pe_78b1). They pasted the PO number in the support form. I forwarded the PO PDF.

Liam B: there are two paths for invoices: API-created invoices (explicit paying_entity_id) and UI-created invoices (select payee from dropdown). The support flow that generates a manual invoice will default to the customer's "primary billing contact" if paying_entity_id is omitted. Looks like support UI defaulted to pe_78b2.

Priya R: if paying_entity_id was wrong, why only the setup_fee is taxed? Shouldn't the whole invoice be taxed if the entity is non-exempt?

Liam B: good Q. Tax engine applies tax classes per product_code. Usage has tax_class="digital_service" which our tax config set to non-taxable for both entities. setup_fee has tax_class="one_time_service" which remains taxable for pe_78b2. So combined effect = single line taxed.

invoice-bot: Automatic note: matched invoice_id INV-2026-03-05 to billing-logs (job 2026-03-05T11:12Z). Tax provider response: {"tax_amount":21.25,"jurisdiction":"NY","rate":0.085}.

Arjun K: next steps to resolve for customer: 1) Issue a corrective credit for tax amount (21.25) and reissue invoice with correct paying_entity_id and tax_total 0.00. 2) Fix support UI so manual invoices preserve explicit payee selection and warn if customer has a reseller cert on any entity.

Maya S: Agreed. I initiated a credit memo in the portal and set it to reference INV-2026-03-05. Created support follow-up telling the customer we'll reissue and waive any late/collection flags.

Liam B: I'll run a quick script to re-generate the invoice with paying_entity_id=pe_78b1 in staging to verify tax_total=0. Command I used: 
```
POST /internal/invoices/regenerate
{ "invoice_id": "INV-2026-03-05", "paying_entity_id":"pe_78b1", "dry_run": true }
```
Expected output: tax_total = 0.00, line_items[1].taxable = false.

Priya R: please attach the dry_run output here so ops can sign off before we reissue live. Also we should add an alert to detect when invoice.payee != customer.primary_reseller_entity while a reseller cert exists.

Liam B: dry_run attached. Output snippet: 
```
{"invoice_id":"INV-2026-03-05","tax_total":0.00,"line_items":[{"code":"usage","amount":1200.0,"taxable":false},{"code":"setup_fee","amount":250.0,"taxable":false}]}
```

Arjun K: great. I've flagged a small product ticket: PROD-4321 "Preserve explicit paying entity on manual invoice creation + reseller-cert check". Priority: P2.

Maya S: Customer replied: "Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm credit and new invoice." I told them timeline ~48hrs.

Priya R: CAUTION — there are a couple of corner cases: 1) If payment already captured and we credit only tax, refunds might route to original payment method and cause bank fees. Ops needs to choose between net-credit vs full refund+recharge. 2) Check accounting rules for VAT vs sales tax (states differ).

Liam B: noted. For this one payment method was ACH (wire) so we can issue net credit without processor fee. I'll coordinate with Finance to post the credit memo and reissue invoice.

Arjun K: Action items summary: 
- Liam: post credit memo and reissue invoice with pe_78b1 (due EOD tomorrow).
- Maya: keep customer updated, confirm when done.
- Priya: add detection rule to billing-monitoring (deploy next week).
- Eng: assign PROD-4321 and include unit/regression tests for manual invoice flow.

Maya S: thanks team :pray: Closing as "escalated — fix in progress". I'll reopen if customer pushes back.
